Write the general term $T_{r+1}$ in the binomial expansion of $\left(\frac{2}{x} - 3x\right)^6$:
$$T_{r+1} = \binom{6}{r}\left(\frac{2}{x}\right)^{6-r}(-3x)^r = \binom{6}{r}2^{6-r}(-3)^r x^{r - (6-r)} = \binom{6}{r}2^{6-r}(-3)^r x^{2r-6}$$

To find the term independent of $x$, set the power of $x$ to $0$:
$$2r - 6 = 0 \implies 2r = 6 \implies r = 3$$

Evaluate the constant term for $r = 3$:
$$\text{Constant term} = \binom{6}{3}2^{6-3}(-3)^3 = 20 \times 8 \times (-27) = -4320$$

In the expansion of $(1 + ax^2)\left(\frac{2}{x} - 3x\right)^6$, the constant term comes from:
$$1 \times (\text{constant term}) + ax^2 \times (\text{term in } x^{-2})$$

Find the term in $x^{-2}$ in $\left(\frac{2}{x} - 3x\right)^6$:
$$2r - 6 = -2 \implies 2r = 4 \implies r = 2$$
$$\text{Coefficient of } x^{-2} = \binom{6}{2}2^{6-2}(-3)^2 = 15 \times 16 \times 9 = 2160$$

Set the total constant term equal to zero:
$$-4320 + a(2160) = 0 \implies 2160a = 4320 \implies a = 2$$
